case_name: Smt. Ganga Bai vs The Divisional Railway Manager

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Smt. Ganga Bai, wife/widow of Surmaji
parties.respondent_defendant: The Divisional Railway Manager, Northern Railway (Delhi Division), Raj Kumar, Sanju, Shiva, Ms. Sevanti, and Smt. Mathura Devi

facts_of_case: Shri Surmaji was an employee of Northern Railway who expired on 19.07.2015. His service benefits were claimed by two women, Mathura Devi and Ganga Bai, who both claimed to be his wife/widow. The trial court rejected their claims and allowed the succession certificate in the names of Surmaji's children.

legal_principles.principle: Children of first wife or second wife are to be treated as legitimate legal heirs.
legal_principles.held: Even otherwise, as per Section 16 of the Hindu Succession Act, the children of first wife or second wife are to be treated as legitimate legal heirs.
cited_cases: Rameshwar Devi vs. State of Bihar

legal_principles.principle: A marriage cannot be recognized unless the first marriage gets dissolved or the first wife dies.
legal_principles.held: Thus, it is evident that the factum of first marriage has been held to be proved by the Ld. Trial Court and only on that ground, the second marriage of Mathura Devi was held null and void but while deciding the claim of Ganga Bai, it was held that she failed to establish her marriage with deceased Surmaji.
cited_cases: Rameshwar Devi vs. State of Bihar

outcome.final_order: The final court order allowed Smt. Ganga Bai's appeal and held that she is the legally wedded wife of late Sh. Surmaji.
